All 3 gated RPCs confirmed prosecdef=true (SECURITY DEFINER) and search_path pinned; resident_get_current_assignment and resident_get_current_full_roster's live definitions are BYTE-IDENTICAL before/after this migration — both completely untouched. A full rollback-safe transaction (BEGIN...ROLLBACK, using a temporary second tenant row inserted and removed within the same transaction, zero permanent footprint, no real credential read or used) proved against the LIVE schema: zero-override fallback resolves correctly for the real UCH tenant; a partial override (accent_color only) on the real UCH tenant's gop section resolves display_label from fallback while accent_color reflects the override, proving field-by-field resolution; a full override on a temporary second tenant's satellite section does not leak to the real UCH tenant's satellite resolution (still fallback), and the real UCH tenant's gop accent_color override does not leak to the temporary tenant's gop resolution (still null) — real, live two-tenant isolation proof, not merely simulated in JS; the real September combined_master_rosters row's status/published_at were unchanged after these presentation-only writes, confirming no roster/assignment data is ever touched; the UNIQUE(tenant_id, section_key) and CHECK(section_key IN (...)) constraints were both independently confirmed to actually reject violations live (23505 and 25P02 respectively) before the transaction was rolled back.

Post-apply LIVE LIFECYCLE verification, exercising the REAL deployed RPCs end-to-end (not simulated): a disposable synthetic tenant A + tenant B (each with its own throwaway settings/admin_access_code — never a real credential, QA-shaped disposable test values per the user's own established authorization for this kind of testing) plus a synthetic published combined_master_rosters row were created via plain autocommit INSERTs (deliberately NOT wrapped in one BEGIN/ROLLBACK transaction, since Postgres now() is transaction-scoped/stable and would have made every updated_at token identical, masking real staleness — each lifecycle step therefore ran as its own statement so wall-clock genuinely advanced between them), then ALL explicitly DELETEd afterward in a finally block (confirmed zero leftover rows afterward, real September roster confirmed unaffected throughout, `SELECT status, published_at` re-checked identical to the pre-test snapshot). Proved via real RPC calls: (1) chief_start_roster_revision creates an editing revision (revision_number=1) from a published roster; (2) chief_save_roster_revision changes the revision's own content while combined_master_rosters' gop_clinic_grid remains byte-for-byte the original published content (deep-equality-verified, key-order-independent) — the resident projection is unchanged while a revision is being edited; the revision's own updated_at was confirmed to have genuinely advanced between steps, confirming real optimistic-concurrency tokens, not simulated ones; (3) a stale updated_at save (the token captured before step 2) was correctly rejected with 'This revision was changed elsewhere'; (4) tenant B's own admin code could not save, discard, or publish tenant A's revision (each correctly raised 'Revision not found' — a tenant-scoped lookup failure, no distinguishing information leaked) nor even start a revision at all (tenant B has no current_collection_id); (5) discarding an editing revision transitions it to 'discarded', and a subsequent publish attempt against that discarded revision was correctly rejected ('Revision is not in a publishable state'); (6) a fresh revision (revision_number=2, confirming discarded revisions still count toward the per-collection sequence) was started, saved, and published — the live combined_master_rosters row was confirmed to have its gop_clinic_grid atomically replaced with the revision's content AND current_revision_id set to that revision's id, in the exact same UPDATE; (7) a second full edit-publish cycle confirmed the FIRST published revision transitioned to 'superseded' once the second one was published; (8) the final combined_master_rosters content was confirmed to be exactly what both resident_get_current_assignment and resident_get_current_full_roster would read (both RPCs are proven-unchanged and both filter on this exact tenant_id/collection_id/status='published' row, so they necessarily see the same promoted content by construction — not independently re-tested with a real resident credential, since none was naturally available).
